active_paradigms.idea: Min-cost flow / bipartite b-matching for exact replica-to-GPU placement given replication counts
active_paradigms.description: Keep the successful water-filling binary search for deciding replication counts per logical expert per layer, but replace the LPT+swap packing step with an exact assignment formulation. For each layer, build a bipartite graph: physical replicas on one side, GPU slots on the other, with edge cost = per-replica token load (weight/logcnt) assigned to a GPU. Minimize the maximum GPU load by solving a balanced b-matching: since all GPUs must receive exactly num_replicas/num_gpus experts, use networkx.min_cost_flow (or scipy.sparse.csgraph with a flow formulation) with convex cost on GPU loads, or iterate linear_sum_assignment on a slot-expanded cost matrix where each GPU's slots carry the same replica cost and the assignment is refined by re-weighting slot costs by current GPU load (a Frank-Wolfe-like reweighting of the assignment cost that steers the Hungarian solution toward min-max). This is exact for the sum objective in one call and approximates min-max through 3-5 cost-reweighting iterations.
active_paradigms.cautions: Per-layer independence must be exploited: the objective decomposes over layers, so solve each layer separately and cheaply. Cost reweighting must be deterministic; cap iterations to stay within the time budget; ensure slot-expansion keeps the matrix small (num_replicas x num_replicas) so linear_sum_assignment stays fast.

active_paradigms.idea: Ruin-and-recreate large neighborhood search driven by linear_sum_assignment
active_paradigms.description: Start from the current best portfolio solution, then run a targeted LNS loop: identify the worst layer(s) (highest per-GPU max load), remove ALL replicas currently on the overloaded GPU plus the lightest GPU of that layer, and re-solve the placement of those replicas jointly with linear_sum_assignment on a reduced cost matrix (replicas x GPU-slots of the two GPUs, cost = replica load, with slot costs biased so the overloaded GPU's slots are penalized by current load). Accept only if the evaluator-aligned objective strictly improves, guaranteeing monotone descent. Iterate over layers in order of max-load until no improvement or a fixed iteration budget (~100 accepted moves). Unlike the failed generic ejection chains and vectorized local search, this uses the exact assignment solver on small subproblems where it is provably optimal for the subproblem.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary evaluator score, with execution time controlled by small subproblem sizes
active_paradigms.cautions: Keep subproblems to 2 GPUs at a time so linear_sum_assignment is O(n^3) on tiny matrices; recompute the full objective incrementally to avoid O(layers) rescans per move; ensure the returned maps (phy2log, rank, logcnt) remain consistent after each accepted move.

active_paradigms.idea: Joint replication-count and placement optimization via per-layer token thresholding with provably optimal count allocation
active_paradigms.description: Instead of the greedy replicate_experts loop (which picks the current max-load expert each time), compute replication counts in closed form per layer: with R redundant experts, the optimal continuous solution satisfies weight_i / c_i = constant T where sum c_i = num_phy; round c_i = max(1, ceil(weight_i / T)) with T found by a single sorted-prefix-sum sweep (O(n log n) exact, no binary search). This differs from the failed analytical water-filling because it enforces the integer constraint exactly via the sorted sweep and handles the count-sum constraint by a greedy repair on the smallest marginal-gain experts. Then place replicas with the existing balanced_packing. Because counts are optimal for the relaxed problem, this gives a tight lower bound on achievable max load that can also be used to early-terminate other searches when a candidate reaches it.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: primary evaluator score via better replication counts; also speed (closed-form vs iterative loop)
active_paradigms.cautions: The sorted-sweep must handle experts with weight below T (count=1) correctly by excluding them from the water-filling pool; verify sum of counts equals num_phy exactly with a deterministic repair step (increment the count of the expert with largest weight/count ratio among count-deficient cases); keep the per-layer loop vectorized where possible.

tried_paradigms.idea: Global (non-hierarchical) rebalancing with multi-start perturbation and best-of-N selection
tried_paradigms.description: The current algorithm always uses the hierarchical policy when num_groups % num_nodes == 0, forcing groups to stay node-local, which can be far from globally optimal when load is skewed across groups. Add a global policy path: treat all logical experts uniformly, compute replication counts via water-filling globally, then pack all physical experts to GPUs with balanced_packing, and compare the resulting objective (e.g., max per-GPU load or sum of squared loads) against the hierarchical result, returning whichever is better. Additionally, add a cheap multi-start: run the packing with a few deterministic perturbations of the sort order (e.g., rotate starting pack offsets, or jitter tie-breaking) and keep the best result by the evaluator-aligned objective computed locally. This is a portfolio approach: since scoring is deterministic, evaluating the true objective inside rebalance_experts and keeping the best of a handful of runs directly improves the score with only linear time cost.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary score via escaping the hierarchical policy's structural constraint; robustness across workload scenarios
tried_paradigms.cautions: Must compute the local objective identically to the evaluator's notion of balance (check evaluator.py's metric — likely max GPU load or variance of per-GPU token counts including replica-count division). Keep total runtime bounded: 3-5 starts maximum, each fully vectorized. Ensure the global path still respects num_gpus divisibility and produces valid logical_to_physical_map with rank indices filling maxlogcnt slots correctly (scatter-based construction already handles this).

tried_paradigms.idea: Massively expand the multi-start portfolio with many deterministic jitter seeds and adaptive time budgeting
tried_paradigms.description: The current program only evaluates 4 candidates. Since the objective function _gpu_load_objective is cheap and vectorized, generate 50-200 candidates by varying the multiplicative jitter pattern (different eps values like 1e-4, 3e-4, 1e-3, 3e-3, 1e-2 and different modular patterns e.g. % 11, % 13, prime-based hashes) across both hierarchical and global policies, plus variations of the swap-refinement iteration count (4, 8, 16, 32). Score each with the evaluator-aligned objective and keep the best. Use a wall-clock budget check (time.monotonic against a self-imposed limit like 200s) to stop generating candidates so runtime never blows the evaluator timeout. Because candidates differ only in tie-breaking, this directly reduces max per-(layer,gpu) load without changing algorithm structure.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: load-balance quality (max per-GPU load) while keeping algorithm runtime bounded
tried_paradigms.cautions: Keep everything in vectorized torch CPU ops with num_threads=1 (evaluator forces single thread); measure objective cost per candidate and cap candidate count accordingly; ensure jitter never reorders weights enough to change hierarchical group packing semantics drastically (keep eps small).

tried_paradigms.idea: Replace greedy max-load replication with water-filling / proportional replication counts decided jointly with placement
tried_paradigms.description: The current replicate_experts greedily replicates the expert with highest weight/logcnt, one replica at a time, which is myopic. Instead, compute replication counts analytically: solve for counts c_i >= 1, sum(c_i) = num_phy that minimize sum over experts of ceil-like imbalance — e.g., water-filling where each expert's effective load weight_i/c_i is driven toward the common target T = total_tokens / num_phy, choosing c_i = max(1, round(weight_i / T)) then fixing the sum by incrementing/decrementing the experts with largest residual weight_i/c_i. Then place replicas with the existing balanced_packing. This decouples the (currently coupled) replication and placement decisions in a principled way and is O(num_log) per layer, fully vectorized.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: balance quality: reduces the max effective per-replica load that placement must then equalize; also faster than the num_redundant sequential loop
tried_paradigms.cautions: Must guarantee all counts >= 1 and sum exactly num_phy - num_log extra; validate the resulting logcnt tensor is consistent with phy2log and rank tensors exactly as the evaluator checks; keep the greedy version as a portfolio fallback candidate since it may win on some workloads.

tried_paradigms.idea: Direct min-max local search on the final GPU assignment: replica moves and swaps across GPUs optimizing the true objective
tried_paradigms.description: After producing the best portfolio candidate, run a refinement pass that operates directly on physical-to-GPU placement: identify the (layer, gpu) with maximum load and the (layer, gpu) with minimum load, and move or swap one physical expert between them whenever it strictly reduces max load (or the sum-of-squares tiebreaker without increasing max). Unlike the existing intra-packing swap (which is constrained to heaviest/lightest pack pairs and equal-count packs), this operates on the final solution with full freedom, including moving a replica to an underloaded GPU even if counts become unequal (per-GPU expert counts need not be exactly equal unless the evaluator enforces it — check and if enforced, use swaps only). Iterate until no improving move exists, vectorized across layers. This is a different failure mode from the earlier numpy local search because it uses the exact evaluator objective, torch vectorization across all layers simultaneously, and starts from an already-strong solution.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: the exact evaluator objective (max per-(layer,gpu) load plus sum-of-squares tiebreaker) — closing the gap between heuristic packing and the true metric
tried_paradigms.cautions: Verify whether the evaluator requires exactly num_replicas/num_gpus experts per GPU; if so restrict to swaps. Keep move evaluation vectorized (compute per-GPU loads once, evaluate all candidate moves as tensor ops) to stay within the runtime budget; cap iterations (e.g., 50 passes) with early exit when max-load stops improving.

tried_paradigms.idea: Direct min-max load balancing via binary search feasibility with scipy linprog (LP-based lower-bound probing)
tried_paradigms.description: Instead of greedy LPT packing of physical experts to GPUs, formulate the final placement as a feasibility LP: given a candidate maximum per-(layer,gpu) load T, each physical replica (with its fixed weight weight/logcnt) must be assigned to exactly one GPU slot, each GPU holds exactly phy_experts_per_gpu replicas, and per-GPU load <= T. Solve with scipy.optimize.linprog (HiGHS) using binary search on T. Since the assignment constraint with slot capacities is an integer program, use the LP relaxation as a guide plus a rounding step: solve the LP, then round fractional assignments with a single scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment call on the cost matrix -log(assignment probability) or on load-based costs, which repairs integrality while respecting the LP's load profile. This directly attacks the min-max objective rather than sum-of-squares proxies, and the LP lower bound tells you when to stop. Process layers independently (rows are independent), which keeps each LP small (num_phy variables x num_gpus*slots constraints).
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: maximum per-(layer, GPU) load — the dominant term in the evaluator objective
tried_paradigms.cautions: Keep LPs per-layer small; cap binary search iterations (~15) and total runtime under the 360s timeout. Use HiGHS method. The rounding via linear_sum_assignment is a single repair call, not multi-stage optimization. Ensure exact slot-count feasibility (num_phy divisible by num_gpus is guaranteed).

tried_paradigms.idea: Joint replication-and-placement optimization by treating replica counts as continuous via water-filling on the LP dual, then lexicographic placement
tried_paradigms.description: The current pipeline decides replication counts (logcnt) first via greedy/water-filling on logical weights, then packs replicas — these two stages are coupled because replicating an expert only helps if its replicas land on different GPUs. Reformulate: for a target max load T, an expert with weight w needs ceil(w/T) replicas (this is the exact LP dual / water-filling solution), computed directly and in closed form per layer. Then total replicas per layer may not equal num_replicas, so adjust T per layer with a per-layer bisection (~20 fast closed-form evaluations, no LP) until sum of ceil(w_i/T) equals num_replicas exactly, distributing the remainder to experts where marginal gain (w/k - w/(k+1)) is largest. This gives provably near-optimal replication counts for the min-max objective. Then placement is a pure balanced-packing problem on weights w_i/ceil(w_i/T), which are all <= T, making the subsequent packing much easier than the current pipeline where replication counts are decoupled from placement. Finish with the existing best-of portfolio selection.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: replication counts (logcnt) optimality with respect to the true min-max objective, plus downstream packing quality
tried_paradigms.cautions: The per-layer bisection on T is closed-form and cheap (numpy ceil/sum), so runtime is fine. Handle ties in marginal gain deterministically. Keep the existing evaluator-aligned objective for final candidate selection. This replaces replicate_experts entirely — do not keep the greedy version as a fallback inside the same candidate unless runtime allows.

tried_paradigms.idea: Simulated-annealing-style large neighborhood reassignment using numpy vectorized ejection chains on the full solution representation
tried_paradigms.description: Rather than pairwise swaps between heaviest/lightest GPUs (which gets stuck in local optima), implement an ejection-chain / cyclic-move local search directly on the phy2log-to-GPU assignment: pick the globally most overloaded (layer, gpu), eject its heaviest replica, insert it into the least-loaded GPU that still has slot capacity, then recursively repair the receiving GPU by ejecting its heaviest replica, chaining up to depth 3-5. Accept moves that decrease max load or leave it equal but decrease sum of squares (plateau walking), and occasionally accept small worsening moves with a deterministic annealing schedule to escape local optima. Vectorize across layers with numpy (all layers run their chains in lockstep with boolean masks), so the per-iteration cost is a handful of O(num_phy) array ops. Run to a fixed iteration budget calibrated to ~60s. Seed from the best current portfolio candidate rather than from scratch.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: escaping local optima in max per-(layer,gpu) load that pairwise swap refinement cannot fix
tried_paradigms.cautions: This is a custom local search but structurally different from the failed 'min-max refinement' (which was simple vectorized swaps): ejection chains with plateau moves and annealing explore a fundamentally larger neighborhood. Keep everything numpy-vectorized to stay within timeout; cap iterations with a wall-clock check. Maintain slot-capacity invariants exactly (each GPU keeps phy_experts_per_gpu replicas) via the eject-then-insert structure. Use a fixed RNG seed for determinism.

tried_paradigms.idea: Exact min-max placement via scipy.optimize.milp (HiGHS) on small per-layer subproblems
tried_paradigms.description: For each layer, formulate the joint replication+placement problem as a MILP: binary variable x[layer, gpu, logical_expert] = number of replicas of expert e on gpu g (bounded integer), constraint that sum over gpus equals the replication count logcnt[e] (which itself can be a variable with sum = num_replicas), and continuous variable T with constraints sum_e x[g,e]*w[e]/logcnt[e] <= T for every gpu. Minimize T. Solve with scipy.optimize.milp (HiGHS backend, mip_rel_gap ~0.01 and a per-layer time cap). For realistic sizes (e.g., 256 logical experts, 8-64 gpus) the LP relaxation of this min-max structure is very tight, so HiGHS converges near-optimally in seconds. Use the existing greedy solution as a warm-start upper bound (via the objective cutoff / node limit) so the solver only needs to prove/improve. Fall back to the current portfolio solution if the solver times out.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Directly minimizes the true per-(layer,gpu) max-load objective, eliminating the greedy LPT gap; also improves the balance metric across all layers.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Cap total runtime well under the 360s evaluation timeout; solve layers independently (they are separable given the objective is max over layers); keep integer bounds tight (replicas per expert <= num_replicas - num_log + 1); always keep the current best solution as fallback; set HiGHS time_limit per layer and threads=1 since evaluation forces single-threaded execution.

tried_paradigms.idea: Min-cost flow formulation of replica placement with networkx.min_cost_flow
tried_paradigms.description: Model each layer's placement as a flow problem: source -> expert nodes with capacity equal to that expert's chosen replica count (cost proportional to w[e]/logcnt[e]), expert nodes -> gpu nodes with unit-capacity edges (each gpu can hold phy_experts_per_gpu experts, enforced by gpu -> sink capacity), gpu -> sink edges carry cost 0. Use networkx.min_cost_flow (or min_cost_flow_cost with successive shortest paths) where edge costs are crafted as convex piecewise loads so the flow automatically equalizes GPU loads — this is the classic flow-based balanced assignment. Iterate 2-3 rounds: after each flow solve, recompute per-GPU loads and update edge costs with marginal penalties (e.g., cost of sending to a heavily loaded gpu grows quadratically), which converges to a near-min-max solution. Replication counts come from the existing water-filling step, so the flow only solves the assignment part optimally.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Improves load balance (primary metric) by replacing greedy LPT packing with an optimal-flow assignment; keeps runtime low since min-cost flow is polynomial.
tried_paradigms.cautions: networkx pure-Python flow can be slow for large graphs — build one graph per layer but batch identical layers (same weight rows) and reuse the solution; keep node count manageable by aggregating experts with identical weights; ensure per-GPU slot capacities are exactly phy_experts_per_gpu; verify the flow integral property gives integer assignments.

tried_paradigms.idea: Layer-similarity clustering with prototype solutions and rank-based assignment
tried_paradigms.description: Exploit the key structural observation that many layers have nearly identical expert load distributions (MoE layers usually share routing statistics). Cluster the weight rows with scipy.cluster.hierarchy (fcluster with a cosine/correlation distance, e.g., threshold 0.05), solve the expensive optimization (the current portfolio + Hungarian refinement) only on cluster medoids/prototypes, then transfer each prototype's phy2log map to all layers in its cluster. Because the objective is a max over layers, transferred solutions are near-optimal for similar layers. This frees a large runtime budget (previously spent per-layer) to instead run a much deeper search (more multi-starts, stronger refinement) on the few distinct prototypes. Finish with a cheap per-layer repair pass: for layers whose max load exceeds the prototype's, run a few targeted swap moves only on the offending GPUs.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Improves the efficiency component of the score (algorithm runtime) by an order of magnitude on layers with similar statistics, while maintaining or improving balance by spending the saved time on deeper optimization of distinct prototypes.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Use correlation distance on normalized weight rows; validate each transferred solution with the evaluator-aligned objective and only accept if within a small tolerance of the per-layer greedy baseline; keep the current per-layer path as fallback for outlier layers; clustering itself must be vectorized (scipy.spatial.distance.pdist) to stay cheap.
